propositions: The test plants a young index.lock and uses threading.Timer to delete it, but on slow runners (macOS py3.13) the timer fires while git holds its own real index.lock, causing git commit to fail with 'unable to write new index file'
The timer body has no identity check and cannot distinguish the test's planted lock from git's real lock, leading to non-deterministic deletion of whichever lock exists at t=0.4
force_reclaim=True bypasses the age gate, so the planted lock is removed on first retry attempt at t≈0, allowing git commit to begin and create its own lock before the timer fires
The production code path is correct and succeeds; the failure is entirely test-local and caused by the test deleting a lock the code legitimately owns mid-operation
The test must be changed to use gitutil._retry_probe (deterministic probe-based release) instead of threading.Timer to release the planted lock only after first failure is confirmed
